steps.text: Part 4 of 4: The rook in a busy position. This part covers Check yourself. Each part is short on purpose: finish one, play a game or take a break, and come back.

Now the unlabelled round. Nothing tells you which piece to think about, and one position will not be a rook at all. For each one: name the piece, walk its lines, stop at the first piece. A wrong answer shows which step you skipped.

steps.prompt: Explain to a friend how to count the rook's squares from d4 in the first position of this lesson, and what changes if a blocker is an enemy rather than your own. Write it in your own words before you read on.

fields.label: A position from this lesson where a piece blocks a rook, and whose piece it is:

steps.text: **Compare.** *Name the piece first, then walk each of its lines outward. A rook stops at the first piece on a line: it stops one short of its own, and may take an enemy piece and stop there. A piece beside the line blocks nothing, and one blocker may cost one extra move.*

steps.prompt: Think of an answer you hesitated on. Which piece was in the way, and was it yours or the enemy's? What will you look at first next time? (optional)
